content: Beclin-1 is a protein encoded by the BECN1 gene in humans. It is the mammalian equivalent of the yeast autophagy-related gene 6 (Atg6) and the BEC-1 gene in the nematode C. elegans. This protein is known to interact with either BCL-2 or class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), and it plays a pivotal role in regulating autophagy and cell death processes. Beclin-1 is critically involved in the development of diseases such as cancer and neurodegenerative disorders. In the context of cancer, Beclin-1 has been shown to influence tumor behavior. For example, ovarian cancer characterized by increased autophagy tends to exhibit less aggressive progression and demonstrates greater sensitivity to chemotherapy. In neurodegenerative conditions, such as schizophrenia, reduced levels of Beclin-1 in the hippocampus have been observed. This reduction leads to impaired autophagy, which subsequently results in increased neuronal cell death. Beclin-1 has been demonstrated to interact with several proteins, including BCL-2, BCL2L2, GOPC, and MAP1LC3A. These interactions are essential for its role in autophagy and cell death regulation.
